  e.g. `read %path%, cache 1 hour sliding`
  e.g. `call LoadUser id=%id%, cache 10 minutes by "user-%id%"`
  e.g. `skip action and set "overridden" as result`
  e.g. `cancel it, value = %mockResponse%`
  e.g. `read file.txt, on error call HandleMissing`
  e.g. `verify %data% with contracts ['C1'], on error call HandleContractError`
  e.g. `save %doc%, on error key Conflict, write out "already exists"`
  e.g. `read %path%, on error 404, write out "missing"`
  e.g. `http get %url%, on error retry 3 times`
  e.g. `http get %url%, on error retry 3 times over 30 seconds`
  e.g. `write out "hi", on error ignore`
  e.g. `delete file 'old.txt', on error 'NotFound' ignore`
  e.g. `call Save, on error retry 2 times, then call Rollback`
  e.g. `call Save, on error call Rollback first, then retry 2 times`
  e.g. `render %template%, on error 404 call Fallback then retry, write to %text%`
  e.g. `before each goal call LogBefore`
  e.g. `after step call TrackAfterStep`
  e.g. `before action file.read call OverrideFileRead`
  e.g. `after action output.write call CaptureWrite`
  e.g. `after each goal call LogAfter, level="info"`
  e.g. `before write on "audit" channel call ApprovalGoal`
  e.g. `on ask on "input" channel call CaptchaGoal, write to %binding%`

  e.g. `call Import, timeout 2 minutes, on error call Alert`

  e.g. `ask user 'what's your name?', write to %name%`
  e.g. `ask 'Allow access? (y/n/a)', write to %answer%`
  e.g. `write out "Welcome back, %user.name%"`
  e.g. `show %message% to the user`
  e.g. `print %result%`
  e.g. `write %error.Message% to "errors" channel`

A setting is read from what it configures, always under `.setting` (`%!app.goal.list.setting.os%`, `%!llm.setting.cache%`, `%!llm.query.setting.cache%`), and changed for this run with `set %!llm.setting.cache% = value` — that is the variable module, never this one.   e.g. `sleep 2 seconds`
  e.g. `pause for half a second before retrying`

  e.g. `render %template%, error=%error%, write to %text%`
  e.g. `render 'layout.html'`

  e.g. `set default %enabled% = true`
  e.g. `set %birthday% = "2026-01-01"`
  e.g. `set %start% = "1st jan 2026"`

  e.g. `set %version% = "2.0"`
  e.g. `set %iso%(duration) = "PT5M"`

  e.g. `set %img% = "real.gif" as image/gif strict`
  e.g. `set %n% = "42" as int`
  e.g. `get 'https://example.com/rates.json', write to %rates%`
  e.g. `hash %password%, write to %passwordHash%`
  e.g. `call GetUser id=%userId%, write to %user%`
  e.g. `sort %names%, write to %sortedNames%`

- variable.set: Assign a value to a named variable, optionally coercing to a type or setting only when unset
  e.g. `set %x% = 5`
  e.g. `set default %enabled% = true`
  e.g. `set %birthday% = "2026-01-01"`
  e.g. `set %start% = "1st jan 2026"`
  e.g. `set %timeout% = "PT30S"`
  e.g. `set %count% = "42"`
  e.g. `set %version% = "2.0"`
  e.g. `set %iso%(duration) = "PT5M"`
  e.g. `set %doc% = "2026-01-01" as text`
  e.g. `set %img% = "real.gif" as image/gif strict`
  e.g. `set %n% = "42" as int`
  e.g. `get 'https://example.com/rates.json', write to %rates%`
  e.g. `hash %password%, write to %passwordHash%`
  e.g. `call GetUser id=%userId%, write to %user%`
  e.g. `sort %names%, write to %sortedNames%`
- goal.call: Call a named goal, injecting parameters into its context, optionally on a different actor
  e.g. `call Finalize`
  e.g. `call ProcessOrder id=%orderId%, retries=3`
  e.g. `call /system/builder/EmitBuildEvent kind="done"`
  e.g. `call goal Render source=%!a.b.c%`
  e.g. `call goal Render module=%!a.b.c%`
  e.g. `if %total% > 5, call MarkBig`
  e.g. `foreach %items%, call HandleItem item=%item%`
  e.g. `read 'config.json', on error call HandleReadError`
  e.g. `call Turn content=%content%, don't wait`
  e.g. `call Backup in parallel`
- loop.foreach: Iterate over Collection, binding each element to Item (and its key or index to Key) and executing the remaining step actions
  e.g. `foreach %items%, call ProcessItem item=%item%`
  e.g. `foreach %rows%, write out %item%`
  e.g. `foreach %products% as %product%, call Handle`
  e.g. `foreach %prices% as %price% with key %sku%, write out "%sku%: %price%"`
  e.g. `foreach %goals% in parallel(cpu: 2), call X, write to %task%`
  e.g. `foreach %orders% in parallel, call Ship, write to %task%`
- goal.return: Return early from the current goal, propagating Data as the goal result
  e.g. `return %result%`
  e.g. `if %goal.IsCached%, return %goal.Cache%`
  e.g. `if %items% is empty, return`
- output.write: Write Data to a named channel — defaults to the actor's output channel.
  e.g. `write out "Welcome back, %user.name%"`
  e.g. `show %message% to the user`
  e.g. `print %result%`
  e.g. `write %error.Message% to "errors" channel`
- on.error: Answer when the action before it fails; optionally retry it, run a recovery, or carry on past the error
  e.g. `read file.txt, on error call HandleMissing`
  e.g. `verify %data% with contracts ['C1'], on error call HandleContractError`
  e.g. `save %doc%, on error key Conflict, write out "already exists"`
  e.g. `read %path%, on error 404, write out "missing"`
  e.g. `http get %url%, on error retry 3 times`
  e.g. `http get %url%, on error retry 3 times over 30 seconds`
  e.g. `write out "hi", on error ignore`
  e.g. `delete file 'old.txt', on error 'NotFound' ignore`
  e.g. `call Save, on error retry 2 times, then call Rollback`
  e.g. `call Save, on error call Rollback first, then retry 2 times`
  e.g. `render %template%, on error 404 call Fallback then retry, write to %text%`
- on.cache: Cache the result of the action before it for a duration; a cached result answers in its place and the work is skipped
  e.g. `get https://example.com/rates, cache for 5 minutes, write to %rates%`
  e.g. `read %path%, cache 1 hour sliding`
  e.g. `call LoadUser id=%id%, cache 10 minutes by "user-%id%"`
- on.timeout: Give the action before it a deadline; past it the action is cancelled and fails with a Timeout (408) error
  e.g. `get %url%, timeout after 10 seconds`
  e.g. `call Import, timeout 2 minutes, on error call Alert`
- condition.if: Evaluate a condition and execute the then-branch actions; pair with elseif/else for full branching
  e.g. `if %count% > 0, call ProcessItems`
  e.g. `if %content% is not empty, call Process`
  e.g. `if %flag%, call Go`
  e.g. `if %done%, return %result%`
- file.read: Read a file's content; optionally resolve %var% patterns in the text before returning
  e.g. `read file.txt, write to %content%`
  e.g. `read 'config/settings.json'`
  e.g. `read 'receipt.txt', load vars, write to %receipt%`

s0_@module.instructions: Step 0 of this goal is `list files in '/logs', pattern "*.log", write to %files%`. Which plang module does the main work of step 0?

s0_variable.set.instructions: Step 0 is `list files in '/logs', pattern "*.log", write to %files%`. Does step 0 use `variable.set`?

criteria.true: the step sets a variable or keeps a result in one: `set %x% = 5`, `set default %x% = …`, `…, write to %x%`
criteria.false: the step keeps no value in a variable

s0_goal.call.instructions: Step 0 is `list files in '/logs', pattern "*.log", write to %files%`. Does step 0 use `goal.call`?

criteria.true: the step itself calls a goal now, alone or inside its condition or loop: `call SendMail to=%x%`, `if %n% > 5, call Big`, `foreach %list%, call X`, `call Compile, on error call Fix` (it calls Compile)
criteria.false: the step calls no goal now; a call that says WHERE the goal runs — `call X in %window%`, `… in %browser%` — runs a page's own function (window.callGoal), not a goal of this app; the goal behind a channel or an event, named to run later, is not called by the step

s0_loop.foreach.instructions: Step 0 is `list files in '/logs', pattern "*.log", write to %files%`. Does step 0 use `loop.foreach`?

criteria.true: the step repeats something for each item of a collection: `foreach %list%, call X item=%item%`, `for each %order% in %orders%, …`
criteria.false: the step does its work once; a list it only reads, counts or passes along is not repeated over

s0_goal.return.instructions: Step 0 is `list files in '/logs', pattern "*.log", write to %files%`. Does step 0 use `goal.return`?

criteria.true: the step returns from the goal, now or as the body of its if: `return %result%`, `if %done%, return`
criteria.false: the step doesn't return; calling another goal is not returning

s0_output.write.instructions: Step 0 is `list files in '/logs', pattern "*.log", write to %files%`. Does step 0 use `output.write`?

criteria.true: the step shows or writes something out, to the user or to a named channel: `write out "Hello"`, `show %message%`, `write %x% to "log" channel`

s0_on.error.instructions: Step 0 is `list files in '/logs', pattern "*.log", write to %files%`. Does step 0 use `on.error`?

How plang is structured:
- A goal is a list of steps. Each step is a sentence saying what to do, written in any human language. There is no syntax and no reserved words; only the intent matters.
- A step is carried out by one or more actions. Every action belongs to exactly one module.
- Within a step the actions form a chain: the result of one action can feed the next one.
- A step may keep its result for later use by naming a variable (a name between % signs). That is the variable module's job, in addition to whatever module did the work.
- `%name%` is a variable — a value the step uses, never words of the step. `%!…%` reads a value from the app itself: `%!app.module.file%` is the file module as a value, `%!llm.setting.cache%` is the llm setting's cache option, `%!data%` is the result of the action before it. The words inside `%…%` are its name, never what the step does.
- In `call X name=value`, `name` is what the called goal reads the value as (`%name%`), even when it is a plang word such as `module`, `file` or `goal`; it is never a module or action of the step.
- A step may guard part of its work behind a condition (condition module), repeat part of it for each item of a collection (loop module), or attach error handling to it (error module). Each of those is an action of its own, and whatever runs INSIDE the guard, the loop or the error handler is also an action of its own — so calling a goal inside an if, a loop or an error handler uses the goal module as well.
- So one step often uses several modules: the one doing the main work; condition/loop/error for a surrounding clause; goal when a goal is called anywhere in it; variable when the result is kept.
- When a condition tests a fact about a FILE or a WEB RESOURCE — whether it exists, is reachable, its size or kind — finding that fact out is the step's main work, and the module that knows the file or the resource is the step's main module; the condition only branches on the answer it gives. (This is only about a file or a resource the step must go and check; a condition that tests a %variable% already in hand brings in no such module, and its main work is whatever it would be without this note.)
- A module counts as used by a step whenever the step's sentence names work that module does, EVEN IF that work only runs in some cases — the body of a condition, of a loop, or of an error handler is named by the step and counts, regardless of whether it happens to run.
- A step that REGISTERS something to happen later — an event handler, a callback, a scheduled goal — does not do that work now. Naming a goal to be run later is not calling it; the step uses the module that does the registering.
- Steps are listed in order and may be indented. An indented step is the body of the step above it, and belongs to that step; each step is still asked about on its own, for what its own sentence does.

These are the plang modules you may choose from:
- condition: Comparisons: ask whether something holds — equal, greater, contains, starts with, empty — and either branch on the answer (if/elseif/else) or keep it. Any yes/no question belongs here, whatever it is about: whether a list holds an item, whether text starts with something, whether a number is bigger. The subject's own module is not involved just because the question is about its contents. What follows the comparison is an ordinary action — call a goal, return from the goal (`if %done%, return`), write out, keep the answer in a variable — and is that action's own module.
  e.g. `compare %a% > %b%, write to %isGreater%`
  e.g. `check if %myList% contains 20, write to %has20%`
  e.g. `check if %name% starts with "plang", write to %isPlang%`
  e.g. `check if %content% is empty, write to %isEmpty%`
  e.g. `else if %a% > 5, write 'mid'`
  e.g. `if %count% > 0, call ProcessItems`
  e.g. `if %content% is not empty, call Process`
  e.g. `if %flag%, call Go`
  e.g. `if %done%, return %result%`
  action condition.compare: Compare two values with an operator and write the boolean result to a variable
    examples: `condition.compare` answers a yes/no question and hands the answer on. The question can be about anything — a number, a text, a list, a file — and the subject's own module is NOT involved just because the question is about its contents. Whatever follows is an ordinary action of its own.

Step text: `compare %a% > %b%, write to %isGreater%`
Properties: `{"Left": "%a%", "Operator": ">", "Right": "%b%"}`

Step text: `check if %myList% contains 20, write to %has20%`
Properties: `{"Left": "%myList%", "Operator": "contains", "Right": 20}` — a question about a list is still a comparison.

Step text: `check if %name% starts with "plang", write to %isPlang%`
Properties: `{"Left": "%name%", "Operator": "startswith", "Right": "plang"}`

Step text: `check if %content% is empty, write to %isEmpty%`
Properties: `{"Left": "%content%", "Operator": "isempty"}` — `isempty` takes no `Right`; the `write to %isEmpty%` keeps the yes/no answer, its own variable.set.
  action condition.else: Fallback branch that executes when all preceding if/elseif conditions are false
  action condition.elseif: Additional condition branch evaluated when the preceding if condition is false
    examples: Step text: `else if %a% > 5, write 'mid'`
Properties: `{"Left": "%a%", "Operator": ">", "Right": 5}` — the write is the body: it goes in the elseif's `child`, `[{"text": "write 'mid'", "action": [output.write]}]`.
  action condition.if: Evaluate a condition and execute the then-branch actions; pair with elseif/else for full branching
    examples: Step text: `if %count% > 0, call ProcessItems`
Properties: `{"Left": "%count%", "Operator": ">", "Right": 0}` — the call is the body: it goes in the if's `child`, `[{"text": "call ProcessItems", "action": [goal.call]}]`, never beside the if.

Step text: `if %content% is not empty, call Process`
Properties: `{"Left": "%content%", "Operator": "isnotempty"}` — the negation is the operator's; `isnotempty` takes no `Right`. The `call Process` is the body, in the if's `child`.

Step text: `if %flag%, call Go`
Properties: `{"Left": "%flag%"}` — a bare `%flag%` is Left's own truth; no Operator, no Right.

Step text: `if %done%, return %result%`
Properties: `{"Left": "%done%"}` — Left's own truth; the return is the body: `condition.if(Left=%done%) { goal.return(Data=%result%) }`, never beside the if.
- file: Read, write, copy, move, delete, list, and check whether files exist through the configured filesystem abstraction. A `%!x.setting%` is a setting, never a file: `save %!llm.setting%` saves a setting, which is the setting module.
  e.g. `check if file.txt exists, write to %fileInfo%`
  e.g. `if 'list.json' exists, write out "there"`
  e.g. `list files in docs/ recursive, write to %files%`
  e.g. `list files in %folder%`
  e.g. `read file.txt, write to %content%`
  e.g. `read 'config/settings.json'`
  e.g. `read 'receipt.txt', load vars, write to %receipt%`
  action file.copy: Copy a file or folder from Source to Destination, optionally overwriting and including subfolders
  action file.delete: Delete a file or directory at Path, optionally recursively; nothing there is NotFound
  action file.exists: Check whether a file or directory exists at Path — what "if '<file>' exists" or "when the file is there" asks — returning the path, whose truthiness is its existence, to feed a condition
    examples: Step text: `check if file.txt exists, write to %fileInfo%`
Properties: `{"Path": "file.txt"}`

Step text: `if 'list.json' exists, write out "there"`
Properties: `{"Path": "list.json"}` — "if <file> exists" is file.exists feeding the condition: file.exists(Path="list.json"); condition.if(Left=%!data%) { output.write(Data="there") }. A quoted file name tested on its own is text (always true) — ask file.exists.
  action file.list: List files in a directory matching an optional glob pattern, optionally recursing into subdirectories
    examples: Step text: `list files in docs/ recursive, write to %files%`
Properties: `{"Path": "docs/", "Recursive": true}`

Step text: `list files in %folder%`
Properties: `{"Path": "%folder%"}` — `Recursive` is absent because the step does not ask for it.
  action file.move: Move or rename a file from Source to Destination, optionally overwriting the target
  action file.read: Read a file's content; optionally resolve %var% patterns in the text before returning
    examples: Step text: `read file.txt, write to %content%`
Properties: `{"Path": "file.txt"}` — the trailing `write to %content%` is its own action.

Step text: `read 'config/settings.json'`
Properties: `{"Path": "config/settings.json"}`

Step text: `read 'receipt.txt', load vars, write to %receipt%`
Properties: `{"Path": "receipt.txt", "Template": "plang"}` — "load vars" (also "fill in the variables", "with variables") makes the file's text a plang template, its %variables% filled from memory; a plain read with none of these leaves Template out. The trailing `write to %receipt%` is its own action.
  action file.save: Write Value to a file at Path, creating directories as needed. Saving a `%!x.setting%` setting (`save %!llm.setting%`) is not this: that is setting.save.
- http: HTTP client: send requests, and upload or download files
  e.g. `get https://api.example.com/rates, write to %rates%`
  e.g. `post https://api.example.com/speech, headers Authorization: "Bearer %key%", body {"model": "tts", "input": "%text%"}, write to %audio%`
  e.g. `upload 'photo.png' to https://api.example.com/images, write to %result%`
  action http.download: Download a URL's bytes, optionally straight to a file (given a path, the body is written there as it arrives). Use this ONLY when the step says **download**, or **save/write a URL to a file or path**. A plain `get`/`fetch`/`post <url>` that reads the response is http.request, not a download.
  action http.request: Send an HTTP request (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, …), optionally with a body — a json object or a dict — and return the parsed response body. Posting data (`post <url>, body {…}`) is a request; only sending a file or form parts is an upload.
    examples: Step text: `get https://api.example.com/rates, write to %rates%`
Properties: `{"Url": "https://api.example.com/rates"}` — GET is the default method; the trailing `write to %rates%` is its own action.

Step text: `post https://api.example.com/speech, headers Authorization: "Bearer %key%", body {"model": "tts", "input": "%text%"}, write to %audio%`
Properties: `{"Url": "https://api.example.com/speech", "Method": "POST", "Header": {"Authorization": "Bearer %key%"}, "Body": {"model": "tts", "input": "%text%"}}` — a json/dict `body` is the request's Body; posting data is a request, never an upload.
  action http.upload: Upload a file or form parts to a URL as multipart/form-data. Only for a file or form part — posting a json or dict body is http.request, not upload.
    examples: Step text: `upload 'photo.png' to https://api.example.com/images, write to %result%`
Properties: `{"Url": "https://api.example.com/images", "Content": "photo.png"}` — a file (or form parts) sent as multipart; the trailing `write to %result%` is its own action.
- ui: Render Liquid templates from inline content or files with PLang variable injection
  e.g. `render 'page.html' with title=%pageTitle%, write to %html%`
  e.g. `render %template%, error=%error%, write to %text%`
  e.g. `render 'layout.html'`
  action ui.render: Render a Liquid template (file or inline) with the current variables and optional explicit parameters
    examples: Step text: `render 'page.html' with title=%pageTitle%, write to %html%`
Properties: `{"Template": "page.html", "Parameter": {title: %pageTitle%}}`

Step text: `render %template%, error=%error%, write to %text%`
Properties: `{"Template": "%template%", "Parameter": {error: %error%}}` — every `name=value` after the template is an argument, even when the value is a variable of the same name: `ui.render(Template=%template%, Parameter={error: %error%})`.

Types
- text — Textual content. Kind is set from the file extension (md, txt, csv, html, ...). Kind is a hint by default; strict is a no-op for text (plain vs markdown is not detectable from content). (e.g. Hello, world)
- number — A number, whole or decimal, of any size. Its kind is the precision it is held in (int, long, decimal, double, …). (e.g. 42)
- bool — True or false. (e.g. true)
- list — An ordered list of values, each of any type. (e.g. [1, 2, 3])
- dict — Named values: each key holds a value of any type. (e.g. {"name":"Ada","age":36})
- variable — A variable, named between % signs, that holds a value. (e.g. %user%)
- item
- type
- status — An outcome's code and its reason (an error's, an http response's); made from a number, its text is the code's standard reason. (e.g. {code: 404, text: "Not Found"})
- duration — A length of time: a number and its unit (200ms, 30s, 5m, 1h, 1d), or ISO 8601 (PT5M). (e.g. 5m)
- choice<errororder> — one of: GoalFirst, RetryFirst
- list<action> — An ordered list of values, each of any type. (e.g. [goal.call(Name="Show")])
- goal — A goal: a named list of steps, called by its name. (e.g. Show)
- choice<actor> — one of: system, user
- parallel

## variable.set(Name: variable, Value: item, Type?: type, Default?: bool = false)
Assign a value to a named variable, optionally coercing to a type or setting only when unset
Name — the variable to set, with its % signs. A `(<kind>)` written after it is not part of the name: it is the Type.
Value — the value as the step writes it, typed as what it is (a quoted date is a date, "42" a number, a label stays text). After another action in the same step it is %!data%.
Type — only when the step forces a type: `as <type>` or `(<kind>)`.
Default — true when the step says "set default", "default to" or "only if unset"; the variable keeps a value it already has

- `set %x% = …` is one variable.set.
- `<action>, write to %x%` is that action followed by variable.set(Name=%x%, Value=%!data%) — its own action, never a modifier, and without a Type.

## ui.render(Template: text, Parameter?: list, IsFile?: bool)
Render a Liquid template (file or inline) with the current variables and optional explicit parameters
Template — the template as the step names it: a file path or the template text itself.
Parameter — the arguments: every `name=value` after the template is one argument, the same as goal.call's (`render x.html, name=%name%, n=5` → name and n). Left out when the step passes none.
IsFile — only when the step says so: `inline` / `as text` → false, `from file` → true. Otherwise left out; the render finds out itself.

## on.error(Status?: status, Key?: text, Message?: text, RetryCount?: number, RetryOver?: duration, Order?: choice<errororder>, Ignore?: bool = false, Recovery?: list<action>)
Answer when the action before it fails; optionally retry it, run a recovery, or carry on past the error
A clause: it comes right after the action it is a clause of, as the next action of the step. It answers when that action fails — after the attempt, so an `on.timeout` deadline is past and an `on.cache` stores only real work.

Recovery — the actions to run when the action fails: what the step says AFTER "on error" (and after any filter like `404`/`key X`). It is the clause's own content, NEVER the action the clause attaches to: `read %path%, on error 404, write out "missing"` → Recovery is `[output.write(Data="missing")]` (the `read` stays the step's action), never `[file.read(...)]`.
Status — handle only errors with this status, written as its code (`on error 404` → `Status=404`).
Key — handle only errors with this key (`on error key "NotFound"`).
Message — handle only errors whose message contains this text.
RetryCount — how many times to run the action again; each retry is a fresh attempt. A retry with no number ("retry", "then retry") means once → `RetryCount=1`; a written number is that number ("retry 3 times" → 3). Left out entirely only when the step says nothing about retrying (then the action is not retried at all).
RetryOver — the time the retries are spread over, a duration ("over 30 seconds" → "30s").
Order — set `GoalFirst` ONLY when the step runs the recovery BEFORE retrying — "call X first, then retry". Left out (the default, retry first) when the step retries then calls — "retry N times, then call X". The word order in the step decides: what the step says first runs first.
Ignore — true when the step says to carry on past the error ("on error ignore", "on error 'NotFound' ignore").

- The recovery runs only on error: it is never also an action of the step.
- Status, Key and Message filter which errors are handled; they never hold what the recovery does. Left out when the step names no filter.
- Several on.error clauses are asked in the order written; the first that matches takes the error, and the others never see it.

## goal.call(Name: goal, Parameter?: list, Actor?: choice<actor>, Parallel?: parallel)
Call a named goal, injecting parameters into its context, optionally on a different actor
Name — the goal to call: the one token right after `call` (or `call goal`), copied exactly as a quoted text — a bare word (`Name="Finalize"`), a `Folder/Goal`, or a `/path/name` (`Name="/system/builder/EmitBuildEvent"`). Never bare (`Name=Finalize`), never an action name like `goal.call`. Only that first token is the name; everything after it is arguments, never the name.
Parameter — the arguments: every `name=value` after the goal name is one argument, its value as written — never part of the name, **even when the value is a dotted variable**: `call goal Render source=%!a.b.c%` → `Name="Render", Parameter={source: %!a.b.c%}`, never `Name=%!a.b.c%`. The word **before** `=` is the argument's name and MUST be kept, **even when it is a plang word** such as `module`, `file` or `goal`: `call goal Render module=%!a.b.c%` → `Parameter={module: %!a.b.c%}` — never a bare `Parameter=%!a.b.c%` (a value with no name binds nothing) and never dropped. Left out only when the step passes no arguments.
Actor — the actor the goal runs on, only when the step names one (`on actor "system"`, `as user`). Not because the goal is a system goal, a sub-goal or a recovery.

How plang is structured:
- A goal is a list of steps. Each step is a sentence saying what to do, written in any human language. There is no syntax and no reserved words; only the intent matters.
- A step is carried out by one or more actions. Every action belongs to exactly one module.
- Within a step the actions form a chain: the result of one action can feed the next one.
- A step may keep its result for later use by naming a variable (a name between % signs). That is the variable module's job, in addition to whatever module did the work.
- `%name%` is a variable — a value the step uses, never words of the step. `%!…%` reads a value from the app itself: `%!app.module.file%` is the file module as a value, `%!llm.setting.cache%` is the llm setting's cache option, `%!data%` is the result of the action before it. The words inside `%…%` are its name, never what the step does.
- In `call X name=value`, `name` is what the called goal reads the value as (`%name%`), even when it is a plang word such as `module`, `file` or `goal`; it is never a module or action of the step.
- A step may guard part of its work behind a condition (condition module), repeat part of it for each item of a collection (loop module), or attach error handling to it (error module). Each of those is an action of its own, and whatever runs INSIDE the guard, the loop or the error handler is also an action of its own — so calling a goal inside an if, a loop or an error handler uses the goal module as well.
- So one step often uses several modules: the one doing the main work; condition/loop/error for a surrounding clause; goal when a goal is called anywhere in it; variable when the result is kept.
- When a condition tests a fact about a FILE or a WEB RESOURCE — whether it exists, is reachable, its size or kind — finding that fact out is the step's main work, and the module that knows the file or the resource is the step's main module; the condition only branches on the answer it gives. (This is only about a file or a resource the step must go and check; a condition that tests a %variable% already in hand brings in no such module, and its main work is whatever it would be without this note.)
- A module counts as used by a step whenever the step's sentence names work that module does, EVEN IF that work only runs in some cases — the body of a condition, of a loop, or of an error handler is named by the step and counts, regardless of whether it happens to run.
- A step that REGISTERS something to happen later — an event handler, a callback, a scheduled goal — does not do that work now. Naming a goal to be run later is not calling it; the step uses the module that does the registering.
- Steps are listed in order and may be indented. An indented step is the body of the step above it, and belongs to that step; each step is still asked about on its own, for what its own sentence does.

How plang is structured:
- A goal is a list of steps. Each step is a sentence saying what to do, written in any human language. There is no syntax and no reserved words; only the intent matters.
- A step is carried out by one or more actions. Every action belongs to exactly one module.
- Within a step the actions form a chain: the result of one action can feed the next one.
- A step may keep its result for later use by naming a variable (a name between % signs). That is the variable module's job, in addition to whatever module did the work.
- `%name%` is a variable — a value the step uses, never words of the step. `%!…%` reads a value from the app itself: `%!app.module.file%` is the file module as a value, `%!llm.setting.cache%` is the llm setting's cache option, `%!data%` is the result of the action before it. The words inside `%…%` are its name, never what the step does.
- In `call X name=value`, `name` is what the called goal reads the value as (`%name%`), even when it is a plang word such as `module`, `file` or `goal`; it is never a module or action of the step.
- A step may guard part of its work behind a condition (condition module), repeat part of it for each item of a collection (loop module), or attach error handling to it (error module). Each of those is an action of its own, and whatever runs INSIDE the guard, the loop or the error handler is also an action of its own — so calling a goal inside an if, a loop or an error handler uses the goal module as well.
- So one step often uses several modules: the one doing the main work; condition/loop/error for a surrounding clause; goal when a goal is called anywhere in it; variable when the result is kept.
- When a condition tests a fact about a FILE or a WEB RESOURCE — whether it exists, is reachable, its size or kind — finding that fact out is the step's main work, and the module that knows the file or the resource is the step's main module; the condition only branches on the answer it gives. (This is only about a file or a resource the step must go and check; a condition that tests a %variable% already in hand brings in no such module, and its main work is whatever it would be without this note.)
- A module counts as used by a step whenever the step's sentence names work that module does, EVEN IF that work only runs in some cases — the body of a condition, of a loop, or of an error handler is named by the step and counts, regardless of whether it happens to run.
- A step that REGISTERS something to happen later — an event handler, a callback, a scheduled goal — does not do that work now. Naming a goal to be run later is not calling it; the step uses the module that does the registering.
- Steps are listed in order and may be indented. An indented step is the body of the step above it, and belongs to that step; each step is still asked about on its own, for what its own sentence does.

Goal, as written:
  Guard
  [0] - if %goal.IsCached%, return %goal.Cache% => decider: goal.return 0.97, condition.if 0.97 => formal: condition.if(Left) { goal.return() }
  [1] - if %items%, write out "There are items" => decider: output.write 0.98, condition.if 0.96 => formal: condition.if(Left) { output.write(Data) }
  [2] - throw %!error%, fix suggestion %hint% => decider: error.throw 1.00 (module error 1.00) => formal: error.throw()

Types
- text — Textual content. Kind is set from the file extension (md, txt, csv, html, ...). Kind is a hint by default; strict is a no-op for text (plain vs markdown is not detectable from content). (e.g. Hello, world)
- number — A number, whole or decimal, of any size. Its kind is the precision it is held in (int, long, decimal, double, …). (e.g. 42)
- bool — True or false. (e.g. true)
- list — An ordered list of values, each of any type. (e.g. [1, 2, 3])
- dict — Named values: each key holds a value of any type. (e.g. {"name":"Ada","age":36})
- item
- choice<operator> — one of: ==, !=, >, <, >=, <=, contains, notcontains, startswith, notstartswith, endswith, notendswith, in, notin, isempty, isnotempty, is, isnot, and, or
- status — An outcome's code and its reason (an error's, an http response's); made from a number, its text is the code's standard reason. (e.g. {code: 404, text: "Not Found"})

## goal.return(Data?: item, Depth?: number = 1)
Return early from the current goal, propagating Data as the goal result
Data — the value the goal returns, given whenever the step names one to return (`return %result%`) — a `%!…%` system variable is a value too (`return %!goal%` → Data=%!goal%). Leave it out, an empty `goal.return()`, only when the step names no value to return.
Depth — how many goal levels to leave; left out unless the step says how far (1 leaves the current goal).

## condition.if(Left: item, Operator?: choice<operator>, Right?: item)
Evaluate a condition and execute the then-branch actions; pair with elseif/else for full branching
Left — the value tested (as the step writes it)
Operator — the comparison, a choice<operator> (a quoted text after one `=` (`Operator="=="`, never `Operator=="=="`); a negation is its own operator; left out when the step names only Left (then the condition is Left's own truth). The table below maps the words.)
Right — what Left is compared to (left out for isempty / isnotempty, and when Operator is)

| the step says | Operator | Right |
|---|---|---|
| `if %x%` alone (is it true, does it exist, is it set) | left out | left out |
| `is 5`, `equals %b%`, `is "x"`, `is true`, `is null` | `Operator="=="` | the value |
| `is not 5`, `does not equal %b%`, `is not null` | `Operator="!="` | the value |
| `is less than`, `is more than`, `is at least`, `is at most` | `Operator="<"`, `">"`, `">="`, `"<="` | the value |
| `contains` / `does not contain` | `Operator="contains"` / `"notcontains"` | the value |
| `starts with` / `does not start with` | `Operator="startswith"` / `"notstartswith"` | the value |
| `ends with` / `does not end with` | `Operator="endswith"` / `"notendswith"` | the value |
| `is in [..]` / `is not in [..]` | `Operator="in"` / `"notin"` | the list |
| `is empty` / `is not empty` | `Operator="isempty"` / `"isnotempty"` | left out |
| `is a number` / `is not a list` | `Operator="is"` / `"isnot"` | the type name: number, list |

`if %name% is "Ingi", write out "hi"` is `condition.if(Left=%name%, Operator="==", Right="Ingi") { output.write(Data="hi") }`.

`if "= %oldHash%" is "= %hash%", call Keep` is `condition.if(Left="= %oldHash%", Operator="==", Right="= %hash%") { goal.call(Name="Keep") }` — each quoted text is a whole operand; the `= ` inside the quotes is part of the text, NOT the operator.

- A quoted text is the whole operand, every symbol inside it included (`"= %oldHash%"` is the text `= %oldHash%`). The operator is the word or symbol BETWEEN the two operands (`is`, `equals`, `>`, `contains`, …), never a character inside a quote.
- `is` and `isnot` take only a type name; a value after "is" is `==`.
- There is no istrue, isfalse, isnull or isnotnull.
- `if '<file>' exists` / `when <file> is there`: a file-existence test asks file.exists first and tests its result — `file.exists(Path='<file>'); condition.if(Left=%!data%) { … }`. A quoted file name on its own is text (always true); never `condition.if(Left='file.json')`.
- `if A and B`: one condition.if cannot hold both. Compare each side with condition.compare, keep each result with variable.set, then one condition.if over the two with Operator `"and"` (or `"or"`).

## output.write(Data: item, channel?: text)
Write Data to a named channel — defaults to the actor's output channel.
Data — what to write, as the step writes it: a quoted text (with or without %variables% in it) is text, a bare %variable% is item.
channel — the name of a registered channel to write to, only when the step names one (`to "log" channel`, `on X channel`, `via X`). Left out otherwise: the actor's output.

- Naming a channel routes the output; it never registers one (that is channel.set).

## error.throw(Message?: text, Data?: item, Status?: status = 400, Key?: text = error, FixSuggestion?: text)
Immediately fail the step with a structured error message, status code, and optional key
Message — the error's message: the quoted text after `throw`.
Data — the values the error carries: the %variables% after `throw` (`throw %!error%` re-raises that error).
Status — the error's status (a number like 404), only when the step gives one.
Key — the error's key, only when the step names one.
FixSuggestion — how the programmer fixes it: the text after `fix suggestion`.

- `throw %!error%` re-raises that error: `Data=%!error%`, never `Message=%!error%`. Message is for a new error's words.

These are the plang modules you may choose from:
- archive: Pack a value, a file or a folder into an archive (gzip, deflate, brotli, tar, tar.gz, zip), and unpack one back — into a folder, with nothing of it landing outside
  e.g. `pack %user%, write to %archived%`
  e.g. `pack /photos to /backup/photos.tar.gz`
  e.g. `pack %report% as brotli, smallest, write to %small%`
  e.g. `unpack %archived%, write to %user%`
  e.g. `unpack /backup/photos.tar.gz into /photos`
  e.g. `unpack %layer% into %rootfs% as oci.layer, at most 2 GiB`
- assert: Test assertions: demand that something holds and fail the step with a descriptive error when it does not. A step that DEMANDS an outcome is this module; a step that merely asks whether something holds, and branches or keeps the answer, is the condition module. Only one of the two is ever used in a step, never both.
- build: Builder internals: load, merge, validate, and save goal and step data during the build pipeline
- callback: Run a callback — resume execution from the Data's Snapshot.
- channel: Manage channels (set, remove) for the current or named actor.
  e.g. `set output channel as MyGoal`
  e.g. `set error channel as ErrorHandler`
  e.g. `set channel "builder" call BuilderChannel`
- code: Manage the provider registry: list, load, remove, and change defaults for signing, crypto, etc.
  e.g. `load code plugin.dll`
  e.g. `code.load Path=plugin.dll, on error key "TypeLoadCollision" call Refused`
- condition: Comparisons: ask whether something holds — equal, greater, contains, starts with, empty — and either branch on the answer (if/elseif/else) or keep it. Any yes/no question belongs here, whatever it is about: whether a list holds an item, whether text starts with something, whether a number is bigger. The subject's own module is not involved just because the question is about its contents. What follows the comparison is an ordinary action — call a goal, return from the goal (`if %done%, return`), write out, keep the answer in a variable — and is that action's own module.
  e.g. `compare %a% > %b%, write to %isGreater%`
  e.g. `check if %myList% contains 20, write to %has20%`
  e.g. `check if %name% starts with "plang", write to %isPlang%`
  e.g. `check if %content% is empty, write to %isEmpty%`
  e.g. `else if %a% > 5, write 'mid'`
  e.g. `if %count% > 0, call ProcessItems`
  e.g. `if %content% is not empty, call Process`
  e.g. `if %flag%, call Go`
  e.g. `if %done%, return %result%`
- crypto: Cryptographic hashing and hash verification using configurable algorithms
  e.g. `hash %content%, write to %hash%`
  e.g. `hash %content% with sha256, write to %hash%`
  e.g. `verify %content% against %hash%, write to %isValid%`
- debug: Write tag metadata onto the current call frame for diagnostics
  e.g. `tag critical=true, owner=checkout`
  e.g. `tag "manual-checkpoint"`
- environment: Run a goal, step, or action on a specified actor
- error: Throw an error from a step (handling one is on.error)
- file: Read, write, copy, move, delete, list, and check whether files exist through the configured filesystem abstraction. A `%!x.setting%` is a setting, never a file: `save %!llm.setting%` saves a setting, which is the setting module.
  e.g. `check if file.txt exists, write to %fileInfo%`
  e.g. `if 'list.json' exists, write out "there"`

  e.g. `read file.txt, write to %content%`
  e.g. `read 'config/settings.json'`
  e.g. `read 'receipt.txt', load vars, write to %receipt%`

  e.g. `call /system/builder/EmitBuildEvent kind="done"`

How plang is structured:
- A goal is a list of steps. Each step is a sentence saying what to do, written in any human language. There is no syntax and no reserved words; only the intent matters.
- A step is carried out by one or more actions. Every action belongs to exactly one module.
- Within a step the actions form a chain: the result of one action can feed the next one.
- A step may keep its result for later use by naming a variable (a name between % signs). That is the variable module's job, in addition to whatever module did the work.
- `%name%` is a variable — a value the step uses, never words of the step. `%!…%` reads a value from the app itself: `%!app.module.file%` is the file module as a value, `%!llm.setting.cache%` is the llm setting's cache option, `%!data%` is the result of the action before it. The words inside `%…%` are its name, never what the step does.
- In `call X name=value`, `name` is what the called goal reads the value as (`%name%`), even when it is a plang word such as `module`, `file` or `goal`; it is never a module or action of the step.
- A step may guard part of its work behind a condition (condition module), repeat part of it for each item of a collection (loop module), or attach error handling to it (error module). Each of those is an action of its own, and whatever runs INSIDE the guard, the loop or the error handler is also an action of its own — so calling a goal inside an if, a loop or an error handler uses the goal module as well.
- So one step often uses several modules: the one doing the main work; condition/loop/error for a surrounding clause; goal when a goal is called anywhere in it; variable when the result is kept.
- When a condition tests a fact about a FILE or a WEB RESOURCE — whether it exists, is reachable, its size or kind — finding that fact out is the step's main work, and the module that knows the file or the resource is the step's main module; the condition only branches on the answer it gives. (This is only about a file or a resource the step must go and check; a condition that tests a %variable% already in hand brings in no such module, and its main work is whatever it would be without this note.)
- A module counts as used by a step whenever the step's sentence names work that module does, EVEN IF that work only runs in some cases — the body of a condition, of a loop, or of an error handler is named by the step and counts, regardless of whether it happens to run.
- A step that REGISTERS something to happen later — an event handler, a callback, a scheduled goal — does not do that work now. Naming a goal to be run later is not calling it; the step uses the module that does the registering.
- Steps are listed in order and may be indented. An indented step is the body of the step above it, and belongs to that step; each step is still asked about on its own, for what its own sentence does.

These are the plang modules you may choose from:
- condition: Comparisons: ask whether something holds — equal, greater, contains, starts with, empty — and either branch on the answer (if/elseif/else) or keep it. Any yes/no question belongs here, whatever it is about: whether a list holds an item, whether text starts with something, whether a number is bigger. The subject's own module is not involved just because the question is about its contents. What follows the comparison is an ordinary action — call a goal, return from the goal (`if %done%, return`), write out, keep the answer in a variable — and is that action's own module.
  e.g. `compare %a% > %b%, write to %isGreater%`
  e.g. `check if %myList% contains 20, write to %has20%`
  e.g. `check if %name% starts with "plang", write to %isPlang%`
  e.g. `check if %content% is empty, write to %isEmpty%`
  e.g. `else if %a% > 5, write 'mid'`
  e.g. `if %count% > 0, call ProcessItems`
  e.g. `if %content% is not empty, call Process`
  e.g. `if %flag%, call Go`
  e.g. `if %done%, return %result%`
  action condition.compare: Compare two values with an operator and write the boolean result to a variable
    examples: `condition.compare` answers a yes/no question and hands the answer on. | `is in [..]` / `is not in [..]` | `Operator="in"` / `"notin"` | the list |
| `is empty` / `is not empty` | `Operator="isempty"` / `"isnotempty"` | left out |

How plang is structured:
- A goal is a list of steps. Each step is a sentence saying what to do, written in any human language. There is no syntax and no reserved words; only the intent matters.
- A step is carried out by one or more actions. Every action belongs to exactly one module.
- Within a step the actions form a chain: the result of one action can feed the next one.
- A step may keep its result for later use by naming a variable (a name between % signs). That is the variable module's job, in addition to whatever module did the work.
- `%name%` is a variable — a value the step uses, never words of the step. `%!…%` reads a value from the app itself: `%!app.module.file%` is the file module as a value, `%!llm.setting.cache%` is the llm setting's cache option, `%!data%` is the result of the action before it. The words inside `%…%` are its name, never what the step does.
- In `call X name=value`, `name` is what the called goal reads the value as (`%name%`), even when it is a plang word such as `module`, `file` or `goal`; it is never a module or action of the step.
- A step may guard part of its work behind a condition (condition module), repeat part of it for each item of a collection (loop module), or attach error handling to it (error module). Each of those is an action of its own, and whatever runs INSIDE the guard, the loop or the error handler is also an action of its own — so calling a goal inside an if, a loop or an error handler uses the goal module as well.
- So one step often uses several modules: the one doing the main work; condition/loop/error for a surrounding clause; goal when a goal is called anywhere in it; variable when the result is kept.
- When a condition tests a fact about a FILE or a WEB RESOURCE — whether it exists, is reachable, its size or kind — finding that fact out is the step's main work, and the module that knows the file or the resource is the step's main module; the condition only branches on the answer it gives. (This is only about a file or a resource the step must go and check; a condition that tests a %variable% already in hand brings in no such module, and its main work is whatever it would be without this note.)
- A module counts as used by a step whenever the step's sentence names work that module does, EVEN IF that work only runs in some cases — the body of a condition, of a loop, or of an error handler is named by the step and counts, regardless of whether it happens to run.
- A step that REGISTERS something to happen later — an event handler, a callback, a scheduled goal — does not do that work now. Naming a goal to be run later is not calling it; the step uses the module that does the registering.
- Steps are listed in order and may be indented. An indented step is the body of the step above it, and belongs to that step; each step is still asked about on its own, for what its own sentence does.

  e.g. `show %message% to the user`
  e.g. `print %result%`
  e.g. `write %error.Message% to "errors" channel`

  e.g. `verify %data% with contracts ['C1'], on error call HandleContractError`
  e.g. `save %doc%, on error key Conflict, write out "already exists"`
  e.g. `read %path%, on error 404, write out "missing"`
  e.g. `http get %url%, on error retry 3 times`
  e.g. `http get %url%, on error retry 3 times over 30 seconds`
  e.g. `write out "hi", on error ignore`
  e.g. `delete file 'old.txt', on error 'NotFound' ignore`
  e.g. `call Save, on error retry 2 times, then call Rollback`
  e.g. `call Save, on error call Rollback first, then retry 2 times`
  e.g. `render %template%, on error 404 call Fallback then retry, write to %text%`

How plang is structured:
- A goal is a list of steps. Each step is a sentence saying what to do, written in any human language. There is no syntax and no reserved words; only the intent matters.
- A step is carried out by one or more actions. Every action belongs to exactly one module.
- Within a step the actions form a chain: the result of one action can feed the next one.
- A step may keep its result for later use by naming a variable (a name between % signs). That is the variable module's job, in addition to whatever module did the work.
- `%name%` is a variable — a value the step uses, never words of the step. `%!…%` reads a value from the app itself: `%!app.module.file%` is the file module as a value, `%!llm.setting.cache%` is the llm setting's cache option, `%!data%` is the result of the action before it. The words inside `%…%` are its name, never what the step does.
- In `call X name=value`, `name` is what the called goal reads the value as (`%name%`), even when it is a plang word such as `module`, `file` or `goal`; it is never a module or action of the step.
- A step may guard part of its work behind a condition (condition module), repeat part of it for each item of a collection (loop module), or attach error handling to it (error module). Each of those is an action of its own, and whatever runs INSIDE the guard, the loop or the error handler is also an action of its own — so calling a goal inside an if, a loop or an error handler uses the goal module as well.
- So one step often uses several modules: the one doing the main work; condition/loop/error for a surrounding clause; goal when a goal is called anywhere in it; variable when the result is kept.
- When a condition tests a fact about a FILE or a WEB RESOURCE — whether it exists, is reachable, its size or kind — finding that fact out is the step's main work, and the module that knows the file or the resource is the step's main module; the condition only branches on the answer it gives. (This is only about a file or a resource the step must go and check; a condition that tests a %variable% already in hand brings in no such module, and its main work is whatever it would be without this note.)
- A module counts as used by a step whenever the step's sentence names work that module does, EVEN IF that work only runs in some cases — the body of a condition, of a loop, or of an error handler is named by the step and counts, regardless of whether it happens to run.
- A step that REGISTERS something to happen later — an event handler, a callback, a scheduled goal — does not do that work now. Naming a goal to be run later is not calling it; the step uses the module that does the registering.
- Steps are listed in order and may be indented. An indented step is the body of the step above it, and belongs to that step; each step is still asked about on its own, for what its own sentence does.

This is a plang goal called Compare. Its steps are numbered from 0.

step 0: if %name% is "Ingi", write out "hi Ingi"
step 1: if %name% equals "Ingi", write out "equal"
step 2: if %name% is not "Ada", write out "not Ada"

These are the plang modules you may choose from:
- condition: Comparisons: ask whether something holds — equal, greater, contains, starts with, empty — and either branch on the answer (if/elseif/else) or keep it. Any yes/no question belongs here, whatever it is about: whether a list holds an item, whether text starts with something, whether a number is bigger. The subject's own module is not involved just because the question is about its contents. What follows the comparison is an ordinary action — call a goal, return from the goal (`if %done%, return`), write out, keep the answer in a variable — and is that action's own module.
  e.g. `compare %a% > %b%, write to %isGreater%`
  e.g. `check if %myList% contains 20, write to %has20%`
  e.g. `check if %name% starts with "plang", write to %isPlang%`
  e.g. `check if %content% is empty, write to %isEmpty%`
  e.g. `else if %a% > 5, write 'mid'`
  e.g. `if %count% > 0, call ProcessItems`
  e.g. `if %content% is not empty, call Process`
  e.g. `if %flag%, call Go`
  e.g. `if %done%, return %result%`
  action condition.compare: Compare two values with an operator and write the boolean result to a variable
    examples: `condition.compare` answers a yes/no question and hands the answer on. The question can be about anything — a number, a text, a list, a file — and the subject's own module is NOT involved just because the question is about its contents. Whatever follows is an ordinary action of its own.

Step text: `compare %a% > %b%, write to %isGreater%`
Properties: `{"Left": "%a%", "Operator": ">", "Right": "%b%"}`

Step text: `check if %myList% contains 20, write to %has20%`
Properties: `{"Left": "%myList%", "Operator": "contains", "Right": 20}` — a question about a list is still a comparison.

Step text: `check if %name% starts with "plang", write to %isPlang%`
Properties: `{"Left": "%name%", "Operator": "startswith", "Right": "plang"}`

Step text: `check if %content% is empty, write to %isEmpty%`
Properties: `{"Left": "%content%", "Operator": "isempty"}` — `isempty` takes no `Right`; the `write to %isEmpty%` keeps the yes/no answer, its own variable.set.
  action condition.else: Fallback branch that executes when all preceding if/elseif conditions are false
  action condition.elseif: Additional condition branch evaluated when the preceding if condition is false
    examples: Step text: `else if %a% > 5, write 'mid'`
Properties: `{"Left": "%a%", "Operator": ">", "Right": 5}` — the write is the body: it goes in the elseif's `child`, `[{"text": "write 'mid'", "action": [output.write]}]`.
  action condition.if: Evaluate a condition and execute the then-branch actions; pair with elseif/else for full branching
    examples: Step text: `if %count% > 0, call ProcessItems`
Properties: `{"Left": "%count%", "Operator": ">", "Right": 0}` — the call is the body: it goes in the if's `child`, `[{"text": "call ProcessItems", "action": [goal.call]}]`, never beside the if.

Step text: `if %content% is not empty, call Process`
Properties: `{"Left": "%content%", "Operator": "isnotempty"}` — the negation is the operator's; `isnotempty` takes no `Right`. The `call Process` is the body, in the if's `child`.

Step text: `if %flag%, call Go`
Properties: `{"Left": "%flag%"}` — a bare `%flag%` is Left's own truth; no Operator, no Right.

Step text: `if %done%, return %result%`
Properties: `{"Left": "%done%"}` — Left's own truth; the return is the body: `condition.if(Left=%done%) { goal.return(Data=%result%) }`, never beside the if.

Types
- text — Textual content. Kind is set from the file extension (md, txt, csv, html, ...). Kind is a hint by default; strict is a no-op for text (plain vs markdown is not detectable from content). (e.g. Hello, world)
- number — A number, whole or decimal, of any size. Its kind is the precision it is held in (int, long, decimal, double, …). (e.g. 42)
- bool — True or false. (e.g. true)
- list — An ordered list of values, each of any type. (e.g. [1, 2, 3])
- dict — Named values: each key holds a value of any type. (e.g. {"name":"Ada","age":36})
- item
- variable — A variable, named between % signs, that holds a value. (e.g. %user%)
- parallel
- goal — A goal: a named list of steps, called by its name. (e.g. Show)
- choice<actor> — one of: system, user

## loop.foreach(Collection: item, Item?: variable = item, Key?: variable, Parallel?: parallel)
Iterate over Collection, binding each element to Item (and its key or index to Key) and executing the remaining step actions
Collection — the list or dict to walk (the collection the step names)
Item — the variable each element is bound to (%item% unless the step names another with `as %name%`)
Key — the variable the key or index is bound to (only when the step names one with `with key %name%`)
Parallel — run the items side by side (`in parallel` → `Parallel=true`; `in parallel(cpu: N)` → `Parallel={cpu: N}`; left out when the step runs the items one after another.)
Returns — the loop's own answer: run one after another, a summary `{count, complete}` (how many ran, whether it finished); run in parallel, the loop's task (awaited later with `wait for`). A `write to %x%` at the end of the step keeps that answer — the loop's, not the per-item work's — so it is most often a parallel loop's task. A sequential loop usually has nothing to write.

- The work done per element is its own action after loop.foreach in the step's list (usually goal.call), never inside it.
- `name=%item%` after the called goal is an argument of that goal.call, not a foreach property.
- A trailing `write to %x%` is the loop's answer (its task or summary). But a `set %x% = <value>` that names the element — `foreach %list%, set %seen% = %item%` — is the per-item work in the body, kept as the step writes it, not the loop's answer.

## goal.call(Name: goal, Parameter?: list, Actor?: choice<actor>, Parallel?: parallel)
Call a named goal, injecting parameters into its context, optionally on a different actor
Name — the goal to call: the one token right after `call` (or `call goal`), copied exactly as a quoted text — a bare word (`Name="Finalize"`), a `Folder/Goal`, or a `/path/name` (`Name="/system/builder/EmitBuildEvent"`). Never bare (`Name=Finalize`), never an action name like `goal.call`. Only that first token is the name; everything after it is arguments, never the name.
Parameter — the arguments: every `name=value` after the goal name is one argument, its value as written — never part of the name, **even when the value is a dotted variable**: `call goal Render source=%!a.b.c%` → `Name="Render", Parameter={source: %!a.b.c%}`, never `Name=%!a.b.c%`. The word **before** `=` is the argument's name and MUST be kept, **even when it is a plang word** such as `module`, `file` or `goal`: `call goal Render module=%!a.b.c%` → `Parameter={module: %!a.b.c%}` — never a bare `Parameter=%!a.b.c%` (a value with no name binds nothing) and never dropped. Left out only when the step passes no arguments.
Actor — the actor the goal runs on, only when the step names one (`on actor "system"`, `as user`). Not because the goal is a system goal, a sub-goal or a recovery.
Parallel — run this call beside the step, answering a task at once (`in parallel` / `don't wait` / `in the background` / `and go on` → `Parallel=true`; `in parallel(cpu: N)` → `Parallel={cpu: N}`; left out when the step waits for the call. (There is no `Wait` property; "don't wait" is `Parallel=true`.))

- The arguments belong to the called goal; they are never properties of goal.call.
- `foreach %list%, call X item=%y%` is loop.foreach, then goal.call with `item` as its argument.
- `call goal X` and `call the goal X` call X: the leading `goal` / `the goal` is only a word, never part of the name or an argument — the same whether X is a bare name, a `Folder/Goal`, or a `/path/name`. `call goal Unmatched action=%item%` → goal.call(Name="Unmatched", Parameter={action: %item%}); `call goal /builder/Build` → goal.call(Name="/builder/Build") (the path is the whole name, `goal` dropped). A name that itself starts with Goal keeps it: `call goal GoalSetup` → Name="GoalSetup".

- A goal is a list of steps. Each step is a sentence saying what to do, written in any human language. There is no syntax and no reserved words; only the intent matters.
- A step is carried out by one or more actions. Every action belongs to exactly one module.
- Within a step the actions form a chain: the result of one action can feed the next one.
- A step may keep its result for later use by naming a variable (a name between % signs). That is the variable module's job, in addition to whatever module did the work.
- `%name%` is a variable — a value the step uses, never words of the step. `%!…%` reads a value from the app itself: `%!app.module.file%` is the file module as a value, `%!llm.setting.cache%` is the llm setting's cache option, `%!data%` is the result of the action before it. The words inside `%…%` are its name, never what the step does.
- In `call X name=value`, `name` is what the called goal reads the value as (`%name%`), even when it is a plang word such as `module`, `file` or `goal`; it is never a module or action of the step.
- A step may guard part of its work behind a condition (condition module), repeat part of it for each item of a collection (loop module), or attach error handling to it (error module). Each of those is an action of its own, and whatever runs INSIDE the guard, the loop or the error handler is also an action of its own — so calling a goal inside an if, a loop or an error handler uses the goal module as well.
- So one step often uses several modules: the one doing the main work; condition/loop/error for a surrounding clause; goal when a goal is called anywhere in it; variable when the result is kept.
- When a condition tests a fact about a FILE or a WEB RESOURCE — whether it exists, is reachable, its size or kind — finding that fact out is the step's main work, and the module that knows the file or the resource is the step's main module; the condition only branches on the answer it gives. (This is only about a file or a resource the step must go and check; a condition that tests a %variable% already in hand brings in no such module, and its main work is whatever it would be without this note.)
- A module counts as used by a step whenever the step's sentence names work that module does, EVEN IF that work only runs in some cases — the body of a condition, of a loop, or of an error handler is named by the step and counts, regardless of whether it happens to run.
- A step that REGISTERS something to happen later — an event handler, a callback, a scheduled goal — does not do that work now. Naming a goal to be run later is not calling it; the step uses the module that does the registering.
- Steps are listed in order and may be indented. An indented step is the body of the step above it, and belongs to that step; each step is still asked about on its own, for what its own sentence does.

This is a plang goal called Page. Its steps are numbered from 0.

step 0: foreach %module.Action%, call goal Unmatched action=%item%
step 1: foreach %list%, call ShowEntry entry=%item%

- archive: Pack a value, a file or a folder into an archive (gzip, deflate, brotli, tar, tar.gz, zip), and unpack one back — into a folder, with nothing of it landing outside

  e.g. `pack /photos to /backup/photos.tar.gz`

  e.g. `unpack /backup/photos.tar.gz into /photos`
  e.g. `unpack %layer% into %rootfs% as oci.layer, at most 2 GiB`
- assert: Test assertions: demand that something holds and fail the step with a descriptive error when it does not. A step that DEMANDS an outcome is this module; a step that merely asks whether something holds, and branches or keeps the answer, is the condition module. Only one of the two is ever used in a step, never both.
- build: Builder internals: load, merge, validate, and save goal and step data during the build pipeline

How plang is structured:
- A goal is a list of steps. Each step is a sentence saying what to do, written in any human language. There is no syntax and no reserved words; only the intent matters.
- A step is carried out by one or more actions. Every action belongs to exactly one module.
- Within a step the actions form a chain: the result of one action can feed the next one.
- A step may keep its result for later use by naming a variable (a name between % signs). That is the variable module's job, in addition to whatever module did the work.
- `%name%` is a variable — a value the step uses, never words of the step. `%!…%` reads a value from the app itself: `%!app.module.file%` is the file module as a value, `%!llm.setting.cache%` is the llm setting's cache option, `%!data%` is the result of the action before it. The words inside `%…%` are its name, never what the step does.
- In `call X name=value`, `name` is what the called goal reads the value as (`%name%`), even when it is a plang word such as `module`, `file` or `goal`; it is never a module or action of the step.
- A step may guard part of its work behind a condition (condition module), repeat part of it for each item of a collection (loop module), or attach error handling to it (error module). Each of those is an action of its own, and whatever runs INSIDE the guard, the loop or the error handler is also an action of its own — so calling a goal inside an if, a loop or an error handler uses the goal module as well.
- So one step often uses several modules: the one doing the main work; condition/loop/error for a surrounding clause; goal when a goal is called anywhere in it; variable when the result is kept.
- When a condition tests a fact about a FILE or a WEB RESOURCE — whether it exists, is reachable, its size or kind — finding that fact out is the step's main work, and the module that knows the file or the resource is the step's main module; the condition only branches on the answer it gives. (This is only about a file or a resource the step must go and check; a condition that tests a %variable% already in hand brings in no such module, and its main work is whatever it would be without this note.)
- A module counts as used by a step whenever the step's sentence names work that module does, EVEN IF that work only runs in some cases — the body of a condition, of a loop, or of an error handler is named by the step and counts, regardless of whether it happens to run.
- A step that REGISTERS something to happen later — an event handler, a callback, a scheduled goal — does not do that work now. Naming a goal to be run later is not calling it; the step uses the module that does the registering.
- Steps are listed in order and may be indented. An indented step is the body of the step above it, and belongs to that step; each step is still asked about on its own, for what its own sentence does.

This is a plang goal called Page. Its steps are numbered from 0.

step 0: foreach %module.Action%, call goal Unmatched action=%item%
step 1: foreach %list%, call ShowEntry entry=%item%
step 2: foreach %products% as %product%, call Ship product=%product%

These are the plang modules you may choose from:
- goal: Goals: call another goal (`call X`, on its own or as the body of an if/foreach/on-error clause) and return from the current goal
  e.g. `call Finalize`
  e.g. `call ProcessOrder id=%orderId%, retries=3`
  e.g. `call /system/builder/EmitBuildEvent kind="done"`
  e.g. `call goal Render source=%!a.b.c%`
  e.g. `call goal Render module=%!a.b.c%`
  e.g. `if %total% > 5, call MarkBig`
  e.g. `foreach %items%, call HandleItem item=%item%`
  e.g. `read 'config.json', on error call HandleReadError`
  e.g. `call Turn content=%content%, don't wait`
  e.g. `call Backup in parallel`
  e.g. `return %result%`
  e.g. `if %goal.IsCached%, return %goal.Cache%`
  e.g. `if %items% is empty, return`
  action goal.call: Call a named goal, injecting parameters into its context, optionally on a different actor
    examples: `goal.call` runs another goal. It is the action behind `call X` wherever that clause appears — on its own, as the body of a condition, as the body of a loop, or inside an error handler. `Name` is the goal; each named argument after it is one row in `Parameter`.

Step text: `call Finalize`
Properties: `{"Name": "Finalize"}`

Step text: `call ProcessOrder id=%orderId%, retries=3`
Properties: `{"Name": "ProcessOrder", "Parameter": [{"name": "id", "value": "%orderId%"}, {"name": "retries", "value": 3}]}`

Step text: `call /system/builder/EmitBuildEvent kind="done"`
Properties: `{"Name": "/system/builder/EmitBuildEvent", "Parameter": [{"name": "kind", "value": "done"}]}` — a path-qualified name is still just the name.

Step text: `call goal Render source=%!a.b.c%`
Properties: `{"Name": "Render", "Parameter": [{"name": "source", "value": "%!a.b.c%"}]}` — the name is the token right after `call goal`; `source=%!a.b.c%` is an argument even though its value is a dotted variable — the variable never becomes the Name.

Step text: `call goal Render module=%!a.b.c%`
Properties: `{"Name": "Render", "Parameter": [{"name": "module", "value": "%!a.b.c%"}]}` — the word before `=` is the argument's name and is kept even when it is a plang word (`module`, `file`, `goal`); never a bare `Parameter` value with no name, never dropped.

Step text: `if %total% > 5, call MarkBig`
Properties: `{"Name": "MarkBig"}` — the condition is its own action; this one is only the call.

Step text: `foreach %items%, call HandleItem item=%item%`
Properties: `{"Name": "HandleItem", "Parameter": [{"name": "item", "value": "%item%"}]}` — the loop is its own action.

Step text: `read 'config.json', on error call HandleReadError`
Properties: `{"Name": "HandleReadError"}` — a goal called inside an error handler is an ordinary call (the read is its own action; the call is in on.error's Recovery).

Step text: `call Turn content=%content%, don't wait`
Properties: `{"Name": "Turn", "Parameter": [{"name": "content", "value": "%content%"}], "Parallel": true}` — "don't wait" / "in the background" / "and go on" is `Parallel=true`: the call runs beside the step and answers a task at once. There is no `Wait` property.

Step text: `call Backup in parallel`
Properties: `{"Name": "Backup", "Parallel": true}` — `in parallel` is the parallel value; `in parallel(cpu: 2)` is `{"cpu": 2}`.
  action goal.return: Return early from the current goal, propagating Data as the goal result
    examples: Step text: `return %result%`
Properties: `{"Data": "%result%"}`

Step text: `if %goal.IsCached%, return %goal.Cache%`
Properties: `{"Data": "%goal.Cache%"}` — the return is the if's body: it goes inside the if's `{ }`, `condition.if(Left=%goal.IsCached%) { goal.return(Data=%goal.Cache%) }`, never beside the if.

Step text: `if %items% is empty, return`
Properties: `{}` — a return that names no value; the body of the if: `condition.if(Left=%items%, Operator="isempty") { goal.return() }`.
